newsitem.title: USA: Los Angeles trade up 14 pct in first half of 1996.
newsitem.headline: Los Angeles trade up 14 pct in first half of 1996.

text.p: International trade through the Los Angeles customs district soared 14 percent to $80.9 billion during the first half of 1996, according to a quarterly report released Wednesday.

Los Angeles remained the nation's busiest customs district, but the gap over New York was narrowing. New York trade was up a solid 20.7 percent to $76.6 billion, according to the CMC-TradeWeek regional trade report.

Detroit and San Francisco, third and fourth in total volume, also posted strong increases in the first half of 1996. Detroit trade was up 11.7 percent to $65.9 billion. San Francisco posted a 25 percent increase to $54.1 billion in total trade, the report said.

Exports to Japan continued to fuel Los Angeles trade growth, jumping 17 percent to $8.3 billion, while imports fell 2.8 percent to $14.4 billion. Trade with mainland China also grew swiftly, up 19.5 percent to $8.9 billion, according to the report.

Top exports from Los Angeles included computer circuits and parts, aircraft, cotton, cars and auto parts. Top imports included computers and parts, cars, telephone and office equipment, footwear and consumer electronics.

The CMC-TradeWeek regional trade report is jointly published by Claremont McKenna College and TradeWeek, a nationally distributed news weekly covering international trade and finance. The report monitors international trade and its impact on the Los Angeles-area economy.
